card: This pull request adds an optional sat_vb boolean option to getmempoolinfo, getnetworkinfo, estimatesmartfee, and estimaterawfee, enabling feerates to be returned in sat/vB instead of BTC/kvB. Today, Bitcoin Core only outputs feerates in BTC/kvB, burdening downstream tooling and wallets that standardly operate in sat/vB and risking integer rounding issues under sub-1 sat/vB fee conditions. Values formatted in sat/vB provide three decimal places of precision via a new ValueFromFeeRate helper. Options can be passed as a dictionary or as top-level named arguments. The change is part of tracking issue #32093 and has no open dependencies.
changed_since_previous: Added a release notes snippet in doc/release-notes-33741.md.
evidence: PR description: "Returning feerates in BTC/kvB it can be very burdensome and is not good practice, as the most widely adopted units are sat/vB."

PR description: "Because of sub 1sat/vB environment we cannot rely on GetFee() because it internally uses FeeFrac EvaluateFee() function which rounds the values to always return an int. If the feerate < 1 then it will be rounded to 1 or 0."
Linked issue #32093 tracks migrating RPC fee rates to sat/vB across the node.
problem: Bitcoin Core fee RPCs return values exclusively in BTC/kvB, whereas modern tooling, wallets, and user interfaces almost universally operate in sat/vB. Downstream clients must manually convert units, adding client-side arithmetic that can suffer precision loss or integer truncation under low-fee (sub-1 sat/vB) conditions.

risk.why: A bug in RPC argument parsing or fee calculation/formatting could break downstream RPC integrations or return incorrect fee rates.

scope_notes: Adds options dictionaries to several RPCs (`getmempoolinfo`, `getnetworkinfo`, `estimaterawfee`) that previously took fewer positional parameters, along with CLI named-argument mapping.
summary: Adds an optional `sat_vb` boolean option to `getmempoolinfo`, `getnetworkinfo`, `estimatesmartfee`, and `estimaterawfee`, allowing callers to receive feerates formatted in sat/vB rather than BTC/kvB. Introduces a `ValueFromFeeRate` helper in `core_io` that formats feerates with three decimal places of precision, avoiding integer rounding issues in sub-1 sat/vB environments. Also adjusts RPC conversion tables and parsing so `sat_vb` and existing estimator options can be passed as named arguments.
